review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner; prospective design self-review
review.decision: Keep an unchanged workbench question visible without queuing another desktop notice after its recorded admission
review.notes: Reviewed the shipped producer, durable attempt timestamps, snapshot publication, and desktop consumer. The regressions use a temporary HOME and fake queue admission. They establish producer behavior and continued scope publication. macOS presentation, withdrawal on a real device, and consumer acknowledgement after admission require separate evidence.

cases.description: An unchanged HQ workspace question has one recorded desktop admission
cases.setup: Synthetic HOME, one user question, a separate verified blocker, and a file containing a previously recorded v1.0.195 attempt for restart coverage.
cases.action: Admit the question, run fresh scans at and beyond the former cooldown, load the old-format timestamp using only files, then give the first matter a different request and resolve it.
cases.expected: The same active request remains in the workspace snapshot and consumes only its first admission. Loading the old timestamp also avoids a repeat. The independent blocker keeps its periodic opportunity and the genuinely new request uses the same matter notification identity. Verified resolution removes only that identity from the active snapshot.

cases.description: A confirmed HQ workspace queue refusal retains a timed retry
cases.setup: Synthetic HOME and a fake desktop queue admitting requests only after the first refusal.
cases.action: Refuse the first request, change the sender to success, scan just before and at the existing cooldown, then scan again after a later cooldown.
cases.expected: Both actual attempts are present in the independent journal. The retry is rate-limited and uses the same matter identity. Once a successful admission is persisted, future unchanged scans keep the request active without another desktop submission.
